FDC 4/9383 ZDC PART 1 OF 2 SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM REFERENCES THE WASHINGTON DC SPECIAL FLIGHT RULES AREA (SFRA). IN ADDITION TO SPECIAL SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS FOR AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS IN THE DC SFRA THAT ARE IN EFFECT PURSUANT TO 14 CODE OF FEDERAL REGULATIONS (CFR) SECTIONS 93.335, 93.337, 93.339, 93.341, 93.343, 93.345, AND 99.7, AND 49 UNITED STATES CODE (USC) SECTION 40103(B)(3) THE FOLLOWING RESTRICTIONS APPLY: A. ALL VFR AIRCRAFT OPERATIONS FROM THE SURFACE UP TO BUT NOT INCLUDING FL180, MUST COMPLY WITH THE FOLLOWING DC SFRA SPEED RESTRICTIONS, EXCLUDING FAA-APPROVED DOD, DHS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND WAIVERED MEDEVAC/AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS: B. WITHIN 30NM OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN INDICATED AIRSPEED OF 180 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS; C. BETWEEN 30NM RADIUS AND 60NM RADIUS OF 385134N0770211W OR THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME, AIRCRAFT MUST MAINTAIN AN AIRSPEED OF 230 KNOTS OR LESS. IF UNABLE, THE PILOT MUST CONTACT THE APPROPRIATE ATC FACILITY AND ADVISE THEM OF THE AIRCRAFTS OPERATIONAL LIMITATIONS PRIOR TO FLYING WITHIN 60NM RADIUS OF THE WASHINGTON DCA VOR/DME; 2409032030-PERM END PART 1 OF 2 FDC 4/9383 ZDC PART 2 OF 2 SECURITY INSTRUCTIONS, WASHINGTON, DC. THIS NOTAM D. SPECIAL AWARENESS TRAINING FOR THE WASHINGTON DC METROPOLITAN AREA IS MANDATORY FOR ALL PILOTS THAT FLY UNDER VFR WITHIN 60NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME (14 CFR PARTS 61 AND 91, EFFECTIVE FEBRUARY 9, 2009). THIS TRAINING IS AVAILABLE IN THE AVIATION LEARNING CENTER AT WWW.FAASAFETY.GOV. IT IS STRONGLY RECOMMENDED THAT ALL PILOTS FLYING UNDER VISUAL FLIGHT RULES (VFR) WITHIN 100NM OF THE DCA VOR/DME ALSO COMPLETE THIS TRAINING. 2409032030-PERM END PART 2 OF 2

properties.title: NW-P-0809-26 · Waterway information - ECHO Program
properties.rawText:
HARO STRAIT AND BOUNDARY PASS – ECHO Program 2025 Voluntary Ship Slowdown
Effective June 15 to November 30, 2026 the ECHO Program voluntary ship slowdown through Haro Strait and Boundary Pass is active for all inbound and outbound commercial and government vessels to reduce underwater noise for at-risk whales. This initiative will remain in effect 24 hours per day until 2359 PDT on November 30, 2026, depending on southern resident killer whale presence in the fall. If it is safe and operationally feasible to do so, commercial and government vessels are requested to not exceed the following speeds through the water:
11 knots – Bulkers, tankers, general cargo vessels, and government vessels; and,
14.5 knots – Vehicle carriers, cruise ships, and container vessels.
This voluntary slowdown takes place between the vessel traffic separation scheme at the south end of Haro Strait at 48-24-22.78 N ,123-12-15.26 W, and the vessel traffic separation scheme at the north end of Boundary Pass at 48-46-39.28 N, 123-1-36.84 W. There are also two optional slow down areas, one rounding Turn Point and the other between Saturna Island and Alden Point, Patos Island.
The ECHO Program is led by the Vancouver Fraser Port Authority in collaboration with government agencies, Indigenous communities, industry partners and environmental groups.
For more detailed information, refer to the following internet web address:
https://www.portvancouver.com/echo/
properties.stationOrArea: Haro Strait, Strait of Georgia, Washington State - San Juan Islands

properties.title: NW-P-0743-26 · Waterway information
properties.rawText:
Effective 0700 UTC JUN 1 2026, to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of Southern Resident Killer Whales (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026, vessels must not approach within a distance of 1000m of a Southern Resident Killer Whale in the Southern Resident Killer Whale critical habitat and British Columbia coastal waters east of Vancouver Island and south of Campbell River (Cape Mudge) and Ucluelet, including Barkley Sound (up to Port Alberni) and Howe Sound, with coordinates listed in Schedule 1 of the Interim Order.
These prohibitions are in effect until May 31st, 2027. Details of vessel exceptions from the approach distance are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 3(2), and 4(2) of the Interim Order. Note that vessels in transit are excepted from the approach distance measure.
Vessels must not operate or navigate within the two Vessel Restricted Zones, specifically those waters off the eastern coast of Saturna Island and southern coast of North Pender Island, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 2 of the Interim Order.
The Vessel Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Vessel Restricted Zone prohibitions are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 5(2) and 6(2) of the Interim Order.
In addition, vessels must adhere to the requirements of two Speed Restricted Zones near Swiftsure Bank, in which all vessels are restricted to a maximum speed of 10 knots over ground, with the coordinates listed in Schedule 3 of the Interim Order.
The Speed Restricted Zones are in effect until November 30th, 2026. Details of vessel exceptions from the Speed Restricted Zones are described in Sections 2(1), 2(2), 7(2) and 8(2) of the Interim Order.
Failure to comply with the Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whales in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 could lead to enforcement action, including fines.
Further details are available at Transport Canada’s website (Interim Order for the Protection of the Southern Resident Killer Whale (Orcinus orca) in the Waters of Southern British Columbia, 2026 (canada.ca), or upon request from a Marine Communications and Traffic Services Centre.

properties.title: NW-C-1839-24 · Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
properties.rawText:
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M11 (downstream of the Bellmouth curve), it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Contrecur hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.

properties.title: NW-C-1838-24 · Waterway information - Calculation of under-keel clearance
properties.rawText:
Canadian Coast Guard Marine Communications and Traffic Services have been using all Canadian Hydrographic Service water-level stations for the calculation of passage authorizations in the SorelMontreal sector of the navigational waterway, namely Sorel, Contrecoeur, Varennes, Montreal-Frontenac and Montreal-Jetty No. 1.
In light of the particular features of the navigational waterway in the portion between buoys M84 (downstream of the municipality of Verchères) and M157 (opposite to the Port of Montreal, section 109) as well as the No. 1 Anchorage Pointe-aux-Tremble, it was agreed to adjust upward the available water column by 10 cm in this portion.
The minimum water column in this portion of the navigational waterway as per the Varennes hydrographic station, obtained after adjustment, will be used for the calculation of under-keel clearance.
Monthly Notice to Mariners Eastern Edition 08/22 refers.

twice as high.

properties.title: OKAC A0488/26 — FIR Airspace Notice
properties.rawText:
Location: ACC/AERODROME CONTROL TOWER (OKAC)

A0488/26 NOTAMR A0429/26 Q) OKAC/QAFAO/I/NBO/E/000/999/2914N04759E999 A) OKAC  PART 1 OF 2  B) 2611141137  C) 2611302359  E) DUE TO OPERATIONAL RESTRICTIONS WITHIN KUWAIT FIR ( OKAC ) : 
 
KUWAIT FIR IS AVAILABLE FOR FLIGHTS ARR OR DEP WITHIN KUWAIT FIR 
SUBJECT TO PRIOR APPROVAL FROM KUWAIT DGCA AIR TRANSPORT DEPARTMENT. 
 
OVERFLIGHT TFC OPERATING BTN BAHRAIN FIR ( OBBB ) 
AND BAGHDAD FIR ( ORBB ) VIA KUWAIT FIR ( OKAC ) 
IS PERMITTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS VIA PUBLISHED ATS ROUTES 
FL 280 AND ABOVE SUBJECT TO PRIOR APPROVAL FROM KUWAIT DGCA AIR 
TRANSPORT DEPARTMENT, FLOW CONTROL MEASURES AND ATC CLEARANCE. 
 
ALL OTHER OVERFLIGHT OPERATIONS THROUGH KUWAIT FIR NOT PERMITTED. 
 
FLIGHTS DEPARTING FROM OR ARRIVING AT AIRPORTS WITHIN KUWAIT FIR 
TO/FROM BAGHDAD FIR ( ORBB ) ARE NOT PERMITTED. 
 
 
DEPARTING TFC FROM AIRPORTS WITHIN KUWAIT FIR 
SHALL USE THE FOLLOWING ROUTING : 
 
A.TFC DESTINED TO AIRPORTS WITHIN OBBB FIR OR OVERFLYING 
 OBBB FIR FOR DESTINATIONS OUTSIDE OBBB FIR SHALL FILE IN ACCORDANCE 
WITH THE NORMAL ROUTING ARRANGEMENTS BETWEEN OKAC AND OBBB FIRS AS 
APPLICABLE TO DESTINATION. 
 
B.TFC DESTINED TO AIRPORTS WITHEN JEDDAH FIR ( OEJD ) OR OVERFLYING 
JEDDAH FIR SHALL FILE VIA NIDAP L550 OR DEKOB P517 OR KATOD G667 OR 
ASVIR H741 AS APPROPRIATE TO DESTINATION. 
 
ARRIVING TFC AIRPORTS END PART 1 OF 2
A0488/26 NOTAMR A0429/26 Q) OKAC/QAFAO/I/NBO/E/000/999/2914N04759E999 A) OKAC  PART 2 OF 2  B) 2611141137  C) 2611302359  E) WITHIN KUWAIT FIR SHALL USE THE FOLLOWING ENTRY 
ROUTES: 
 
A.TFC ARRIVING FROM OBBB FIR SHALL FILE VIA KUMBO A453. 
 
B.TFC ARRIVING FROM OEJD FIR SHALL FILE VIA KUNRU P891 OR SOROR A788 
OR H741 ASVIR. 
 
OPERATORS SHALL CARRY SUFFICIENT FUEL TO ACCOMMODATE POSSIBLE DELAYS 
OR DIVERSION REQUIREMENTS DUE TO TACTICAL REASONS. END PART 2 OF 2

NW-463-26 (Kattegat)

Denmark. Kattegat. Øster Flak SE. Firing exercise.

Firing exercise

On 21 November from 0800 UTC to 1200 UTC, a firing exercise will be held from HDMS NYMFEN (DANISH WARSHIP P524) on pos . 56° 53.0'N - 011° 05.0'E
Live ordnance will be used.
Military guard vessels will be present and can be contacted on VHF CH 16 and 06.
Mariners are advised to keep a safety distance of 5nm.

properties.rawText:
NOTAM Number :
FDC 6/9141
Download shapefiles
Issue Date :
November 20, 2026 at 1435 UTC
Location :
Middleburg, Virginia near ARMEL VOR/DME (AML)
Beginning Date and Time :
November 21, 2026 at 1830 UTC
Ending Date and Time :
November 22, 2026 at 2300 UTC
Reason for NOTAM :
Temporary flight restrictions for VIP Movement
Type :
VIP
Replaced NOTAM(s) :
N/A
Affected Area(s)
Airspace Definition:
Center:
On the ARMEL VOR/DME (AML) 286 degree radial at 13.7 nautical miles. (Latitude: 38º57'53"N, Longitude: 77º45'21"W)
Radius:
5 nautical miles
Altitude:
From the surface up to and including 4999 feet AGL
Effective Date(s):
From November 21, 2026 at 1830 UTC (November 21, 2026 at 1330 EST)
To November 22, 2026 at 2300 UTC (November 22, 2026 at 1800 EST)
Operating Restrictions and Requirements
No pilots may operate an aircraft in the areas covered by this NOTAM (except as described).
EXC THE FLT OPS LISTED BLW:
ACFT MUST BE SQUAWKING AN ATC DISCRETE BEACON CODE AT ALL TIMES WHILE IN THE TFR AND MUST REMAIN IN TWO-WAY RADIO COM WITH ATC.
LAW ENFORCEMENT, FIREFIGHTING, AND MEDEVAC/AIR AMBULANCE FLIGHTS ON ACT MISSIONS.
TRANSIENT OPS ARE AUTH FOR SAFETY OF FLT OR TO MEET OPERATIONAL DEMANDS.
ACFT MAY NOT LOITER.
UAS OPR WHO DO NOT COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE AIRSPACE RESTRICTIONS ARE WARNED THAT PURSUANT TO 10 U.S.C.SECTION 130I AND 6 U.S.C.SECTION 124N, THE DEPARTMENT OF DEFENSE(DOD), THE DEPARTMENT OF HOMELAND SECURITY(DHS) OR THE DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE(DOJ) MAY TAKE SECURITY ACTION THAT RESULTS IN THE INTERFERENCE, DISRUPTION, SEIZURE, DAMAGING, OR DESTRUCTION OF UNMANNED ACFT DEEMED TO POSE A CREDIBLE SAFETY OR SECURITY THREAT TO PROTECTED PERSONNEL, FAC, OR ASSETS.
THE SYSTEM OPERATIONS SUPPORT CENTER (SOSC), IS THE CDN FAC FOR UAS OPS, SUBMIT SGI WAIVER REQUEST VIA HTTPS://WAIVERS.FAA.GOV, FIRST RESPONDERS EMGERGENCY OPS CTC THE SOSC AT 202-267-8276.
THE FAA RECOMMENDS THAT ALL ACFT OPR CK NOTAMS FREQUENTLY FOR POSSIBLE CHANGES TO THIS TFR PRIOR TO OPS. OPR MAY REVIEW THE TFR DETAILS AT HTTPS://TFR.FAA.GOV/ OR HTTPS://WWW.1800WXBRIEF.COM.
Other Information:

ZDC - Washington Center
Authority:

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 20 at 3:20PM MST until November 27 at 3:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ

* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 315 PM MST Friday Nov 27.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 313 PM MST, a streamflow gauge has indicated that water from
an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard in Clyde River for Saturday.

Falling snow and strong northwest winds of 60 gusting up to 80 km/h has yielded to  blizzard conditions in Clyde River for Saturday. Blizzard conditions will improve Saturday late evening or overnight has winds gradually become lighter.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:24AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through mid next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

.Heavy rainfall has allowed the St Johns River at Sanford to continue

through Moderate Flood Stage this weekend, with additional rises
anticipated thereafter, reaching Major Flood Stage by the middle of

Seminole counties, including Sanford, Enterprise and Lake Monroe.

at 7:30 AM EST Saturday was 6.9 feet.

properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 21 at 12:38AM PST until November 21 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

* WHAT...For the Gale Warning, southeast winds 25 to 35 kt. For
the Small Craft Advisory, southeast winds 20 to 30 kt and seas 8
to 12 ft.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters From Cape Flattery To James Island 10
To 60 Nm.

* WHEN...For the Gale Warning, until 4 PM PST this afternoon.
For the Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM
PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

A Gale Warning means winds of 34 to 47 knots are imminent or
occurring. Operating a vessel in gale conditions requires
experience and properly equipped vessels. It is highly
recommended that mariners without the proper experience seek safe
harbor prior to the onset of gale conditions.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Heavy snowfall expected Sunday.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 10 to 20 cm.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Beginning Sunday morning and ending Sunday evening.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking northeast across the region will bring heavy snow. A snowfall warning may be issued as the event approaches. 

Allow extra time for travel. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 21 at 3:46PM EST until November 21 at 4:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

SMWMLB

The National Weather Service in Melbourne has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm...

* Until 445 PM EST.

* At 346 PM EST, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line from 43 NM northeast of Hobe
Sound Beach to 41 NM east of Jupiter Island, or along a line from
43 NM east of Saint Lucie Nuclear Power Plant to 41 NM east of
Jupiter Island, moving north at 30 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts 34 knots or greater, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.
Wind gusts 34 knots or greater, high waves, dangerous lightning, and
heavy rain are possible with these storms.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
properties.stationOrArea: Sebastian Inlet to Jupiter Inlet 20-60 nm

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 21 at 2:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin, in combination
with strong north-northeast flow, has caused river levels on The St
Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. Continued rises
through Major Flood Stage are forecast through the middle of next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering
many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration
flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return
below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road
becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous
homes on Wildhog, Possum, and Bonnet roads. Roads along Blue Creek
are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and
Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are
inaccessible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 4.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

911 reported people trapped in vehicles and swept by water surges in
the area.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard continues at Clyde River tonight.

Falling snow and strong northwesterly winds of 60 gusting to 80 km/h continues to cause near-zero visibilities in blowing snow.

Conditions will improve overnight Saturday or early Sunday morning as winds diminish.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. If you become lost or stranded, remain where you are until conditions improve.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
properties.rawText:
Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 21 at 8:12PM EST until November 21 at 8:45PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

At 812 PM EST, a severe thunderstorm was located over Vero Beach
Highland, or near Vero Beach South, moving northeast at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and small hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Vero Beach, Indian River Shores, Vero Beach South, Gifford, Indrio,
Vero Beach Highland, Pointe West, Lakewood Park, South Beach,
Queens Cove, Grovenor Estates, Florida Ridge, Vero Beach Airport,
Floralton Beach, Moorings Of Vero Beach and Jaycee Beach.

Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

A Tornado Watch remains in effect until 1000 PM EST for a portion of
east central Florida.

Northwestern Martin County in east central Florida...

Southwestern St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* Until 815 PM EST.

* Locations impacted include...

windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds.

structure.

east central Florida.

* WHEN...Until 1000 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 658 PM AST, emergency management reported flooding due to Rio
Culebrinas out of its banks affecting PR-110, km 9.9, near Valle
Encantado in Sector Los Cocos. The road is now closed. Between 2
and 4 inches of rain fell earlier today.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 21 at 6:49PM AST until November 21 at 9:45PM AST by NWS San Juan PR

* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
occurring.

* WHERE...Naguabo...

* WHEN...Until 945 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable. Expect
many areas of slow moving or standing water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 644 PM AST, emergency management reported flooding in PR-31,
Exit 22 toward Highway PR-53. Flooding is already occurring and
the road is now closed. They reported that PR-973 is also closed.
Between 3 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the
warned area.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy snowfall expected Sunday.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 15 to 25 cm over western portions of the region including Hearst.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Beginning Sunday morning and ending Sunday evening.

Additional information:
Rain across the region will transition to heavy snow Sunday morning. During this transition, there is a risk of brief freezing rain. 

In eastern portions of the region, including Smooth Rock Falls, the transition to snow will occur later Sunday afternoon or Sunday evening.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times. Local utility outages are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning
properties.rawText:
Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued November 22 at 1:47AM CST until November 22 at 2:15AM CST by NWS Norman OK

SVROUN

The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Western Oklahoma County in central Oklahoma...
Northeastern Canadian County in central Oklahoma...

* Until 215 AM CST.

* At 147 AM CST, a severe thunderstorm was located near El Reno,
moving east at 50 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and penny size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Oklahoma City, southwestern Edmond, Del City, El Reno, Yukon,
Bethany, Warr Acres, The Village, Piedmont, Nichols Hills, Concho,
Forest Park, Woodlawn Park, Lake Aluma, Smith Village, and
Richland.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 21 at 10:46PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX

Areas of fog with visibility of 2 NM or less will be possible
over the Galveston Bay, with the lowest visibility across the
upper part of the Bay, including the Houston Ship Channel through
early Sunday morning. Mariners should be prepared for abrupt
visibility changes down to 1 NM or less. A Dense Fog Advisory
may be needed if visibility drops to and remains at or below 1 NM.


Mariners should exercise caution, reduce speeds, and be prepared
for sudden drops in visibility.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:36PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has maintained a steady climb through Moderate Flood
Stage on the St Johns River at Deland, with river levels forecast to
reach Major Flood Stage late this weekend. A steady rise through
Major Flood Stage is anticipated through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 5.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 5.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise into Major Flood Stage
early next week, reaching 6.0 feet mid week. Additional rises are
possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Sunday afternoon at noon EST.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. Continued
rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through this weekend.
River levels may begin to slowly decline next week while remaining in
Major Flood Stage.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 12.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 12.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 13.0 feet
this weekend, with a slow and steady decline forecast thereafter.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to reach Major Flood Stage, well above
its previous record flood stage. The river level will remain steady
into the middle of next week, with a chance for the start of a slow
decline late next week.

area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 21 at 8:21PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage.
Continued rises through Major Flood Stage are forecast through next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Saturday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Saturday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to gradually rise through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 4.3 feet into the middle of next week.
Additional rises thereafter will be possible.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 22 at 9:21AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused river
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage.
The river may hold steady early this week with continued rises
through Major Flood Stage then forecast mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Sunday the stage was 4.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Sunday was 4.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to hold steady near 4.1 feet
early this week with continued rises through Major Flood Stage
forecast mid to late week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Freezing rain is possible starting this afternoon.

What:
Freezing rain with a few millimetres of ice build up is possible.

When:
Beginning this afternoon and ending late this evening.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking northeast across the region may bring several hours of freezing rain. There remains a high degree of uncertainty as to whether or not any freezing will develop over the region.  A freezing rain warning may be issued later today if confidence increases. 

Allow extra time for travel. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: special weather statement

Possibility of freezing rain on the Billy-Diamond Highway on Sunday

What:
Freezing rain that could make surfaces slippery.

When:
Sunday afternoon and Sunday evening.

Where:

Additional information:
Possibility of 5 to 10 millimeters of freezing rain. The freezing rainfall rate could reach 2 millimeters per hour on Sunday evening.

Travel conditions may be difficult. Icy surfaces may be hard to spot.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy snowfall expected today.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 15 to 25 cm over western portions of the region including Hearst.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Beginning late this morning or early this afternoon and ending Sunday night.

Additional information:
Rain across the region will transition to heavy snow late this morning or early this afternoon. During this transition, there is a risk of ice pellets or brief freezing rain. 

In eastern portions of the region, including Kapuskasing and Smooth Rock Falls, the transition to snow will occur later this afternoon or early this evening. Total accumulations here are expected to be on the low end of the range.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times. Local utility outages are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

Marine Weather Statement issued November 22 at 4:59PM AST by NWS San Juan PR

A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N...

* At 459 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated strong thunderstorms,
capable of producing winds to around 30 knots. These strong
thunderstorms were located over open waters of Atlantic Waters of
Puerto Rico and USVI from 10 NM to 19.5N zone, moving north at 15
knots.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly open waters of Atlantic Waters of Puerto Rico and USVI from
10 NM to 19.5N.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
office.

Mariners can expect gusty winds to around 30 knots, locally higher
waves, lightning strikes, and heavy downpours. Boaters should seek
safe harbor immediately until these storms pass.

waterspouts was located 27 nm southeast of Atlas Tanker, moving
northeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this storm passes.
Wind gusts to 40 knots, high waves, dangerous lightning, and heavy
rain are possible with this storm.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 22 at 12:03PM CST by NWS Houston/Galveston TX

Lingering pockets of dense fog continue to loom across portions
of the lower bays and gulf coast this afternoon. Galveston harbor
and areas along Bolivar are currently experiences the worst
impacts to visibility. Satellite imagery shows low stratus/fog
shifting southward with a pocket of clearer skies following it.
Visibility should slowly improve, generally north to south, over
the next few hours. However, mariners should continue to exercise
caution when navigating these isolated pockets of dense fog.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 22 at 7:39PM CST until November 22 at 8:15PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX

For the following areas...
Coastal waters from Baffin Bay to Port Mansfield TX out 20 NM...

At 739 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing waterspouts
was located 23 nm south of Malaquite Beach, or 30 nm north of Laguna
Madre, moving southeast at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to nearly 50 knots.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Frequent lightning is occurring with this storm. If caught on the
open water stay below deck if possible, keep away from ungrounded
metal objects.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 22 at 2:21PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

FRONTAL PASSAGE WILL BRING THE POTENTIAL FOR HEAVIER SHOWERS AND
ISOLATED THUNDERSTORMS TO THE COASTAL WATERS NOW THROUGH THIS
EVENING

A moist and unstable air mass will bring the potential for heavier
showers and isolated thunderstorms to the coastal waters. Any
thunderstorm or stronger shower that form will be capable of
producing locally gale force winds and rough seas, dangerous
lightning, heavy rainfall with reduced visibility, and a remote
risk of a waterspout.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Freezing rain possible.

What:
Freezing rain with a few millimetres of ice build up is possible.

When:
Continuing this evening.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking northeast across the region may bring several hours of freezing rain. There remains a high degree of uncertainty as to whether or not any freezing will develop over the region. 

Allow extra time for travel. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog continues in Norman Wells.

Conditions are expected to remain poor before dissipating on Monday afternoon.

Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

Be prepared for areas of near-zero visibility and allow extra time to reach your destination.

Fog advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in fog is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NTstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NTStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy snowfall continues.

What:
Snow with total amounts of 15 to 25 cm over western portions of the region including Hearst.
Reduced visibility in heavy snow.

When:
Continuing tonight.

Additional information:
Snow will continue across the region tonight easing off to periods of light snow by Monday morning.

In eastern portions of the region, including Kapuskasing and Smooth Rock Falls, total accumulations are expected to be on the low end of the range due to the late transition from rain to snow.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times. Local utility outages are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

A period of strong winds are expected.

When: Monday afternoon and evening.

Where: Exposed coastal areas bordering Hecate Strait near Sandspit.

Remarks: A strong frontal system will approach Haida Gwaii on Monday resulting in very strong winds over the region. 

Strong winds will prevail through the period with gusts of 110 km/h at times.

Secure loose objects. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

When: Midnight tonight through to Tuesday afternoon.

Where: Inland areas of east Vancouver Island including North Courtenay, Cumberland, Campbell River, Highway 19.

Remarks: A strong frontal system sets up off the West Coast tonight through Tuesday night bringing heavy rain and strong winds to the region. Inland areas of Vancouver Island are expected to see 50 to 80 mm by Tuesday morning with more possible during the day.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas.

Allow extra time for travel.

properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 23 at 1:08AM PST until November 24 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR

* WHAT...South winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and
steep seas 10 to 13 ft at 13 seconds through tonight. South
winds increase late tonight to gales 30 to 40 kt with gusts up
to 50 kt with very steep and hazardous seas 17 to 22 ft at 13
seconds expected. Isolated areas of storm force gusts are
possible Tuesday morning and afternoon.

* WHERE...All areas, though the strongest winds are expected
south of Cape Arago.

* WHEN...For the Small Craft Advisory, until 7 AM PST Monday.
For the Gale Warning, from 7 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds and very steep seas could capsize or
damage vessels. Low visibility conditions are expected.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid strong winds and very steep
seas. Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or
secure the vessel for severe conditions.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 22 at 9:31PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to
reach Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue a gradual
rise through the week, and may approach its record flood.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Sunday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Sunday was 5.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.1 feet late this
week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Heavy rainfall is expected.

Locations: Nova Scotia.

Potential rainfall: 30 to 50 mm, possibly higher over some areas.

Potential wind gusts: 70 to 80 km/h along the Atlantic coast.

Time span: this morning until early this evening.

Remarks: A moisture-laden air mass will contribute to enhanced rainfall, accumulations are expected to be highly variable over short distances. Localized flooding may occur in low-lying areas.

Clear storm drains and gutters of leaves and other debris in advance of the rainfall.

properties.title: Yellow warning · smog warning
properties.rawText:
High concentration of pollutants are expected and will result in poor air quality, especially in urban areas where pollutant emissions are higher.

High concentrations of pollutants are expected to persist into the night.

In Quebec, wood heating is the main source of fine particles that contribute to smog during winter. This activity generates the largest number of these particulates, more than industrial activities and transportation. Please consult your municipality's website to find out if there are any rules governing the use of wood-burning stoves or fireplaces in your community.

Additional information:

To learn more about the Info-Smog program, go to Environment Canada’s website at https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/info-smog.html.

For air quality indexes in Quebec, visit the website of the Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques at https://www.iqa.environnement.gouv.qc.ca/contenu/index_en.asp.

For the air quality index in Montréal, visit the Réseau de surveillance de la qualité de l’air de la Ville de Montréal’s website at https://montreal.ca/en/topics/air-quality.

To learn more about the effects of smog on your health in Québec, visit the Ministère de la Santé et des Services sociaux’s website at https://www.quebec.ca/en/health. You can also visit the Direction régionale de santé publique de Montréal at https://santemontreal.qc.ca/en/public/.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

properties.rawText:
What:
Total snowfall accumulations of 15 to 20 centimeters are expected.

When:
Into Monday morning

Where:
Waskaganish

Additional information: Close to 5 centimetres of snow are expected tonight.

Additionally, up to 5 millimetres of freezing rain are possible along the Billy-Diamond Highway north of kilometre 135 this evening. Icy surfaces may be hard to spot.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Allow extra time for travel.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:59AM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 856 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 2.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 11:36 AM
Mon 11/23, 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, 2.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26.
* West Sacramento: 2.2 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 2:49
PM Mon 11/23, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM
Tue 11/24, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.4 ft at 2:00 PM Mon 11/23,
+7.5 ft at 2:45 PM Tue 11/24, +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.6 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 23 at 10:29AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast hold near a crest today before beginning a very slow
decline within Major flood stage later in the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river has surpassed its previous record flood.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EST Monday, November 23 the stage was 13.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:45 AM AM EST Monday was 13.1 feet.
- Forecast...River levels are forecast hold near a crest of 13.1
feet today before beginning a very slow decline within Major
flood stage later in the week.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

on the St Johns River at Astor to rise into Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid to late week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth

inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

properties.title: Marine Weather Statement
properties.rawText:
Marine Weather Statement issued November 23 at 3:27AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA

RISK OF BREAKING WAVES IN THE MORRO BAY AND VENTURA HARBOR
ENTRRANCES EARLY WEDNESDAY MORNING THROUGH THURSDAY AFTERNOON

A large and long period westerly swell will produce a risk of
breaking waves in the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances
early Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. These
conditions have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes
resulting in serious injury or death, even to the most experienced
mariners.

Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances during
the time mentioned. For more information, contact the local
harbor patrol or coast guard station and continue to monitor NOAA
Weather Radio for the latest weather information.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow.
Local snowfall amounts of 5 cm.

When:
Tonight into early Tuesday morning.

Additional Information:
Lake effect showers and flurries off Lake Huron are expected to intensify and fully change over to snow this evening. Although snowfall amounts are not expected to be significant, visibility may very poor under lake effect snow bands. Conditions are expected to improve Tuesday morning.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly. Visibility may be suddenly reduced at times in heavy snow.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. If visibility is reduced while driving, slow down, watch for tail lights ahead and be prepared to stop.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

Lake effect snow off Georgian Bay tonight.

What:
Local snowfall amounts of 5 to 10 cm.
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

A period of strong winds are expected.

When: This afternoon and evening.

Where: Exposed coastal areas bordering Hecate Strait near Sandspit.

Remarks: A strong frontal system will approach Haida Gwaii today resulting in very strong winds over the region. 

Very strong winds will prevail through the period with gusts of 110 km/h at times. The very strong winds will ease slightly later this evening, but will intensify overnight and continue strong into Tuesday.

Secure loose objects. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning

Damaging winds are expected.

A period of strong winds are expected.

When: This afternoon and evening.

Where: Exposed coastal areas of Northern Vancouver Island.

Remarks: A vigorous frontal system will approach Vancouver Island today resulting in very strong winds over the region. 

Intense winds will prevail through the period with gusts of 110 km/h at times. The winds will ease slightly later this evening, but will remain strong into Tuesday.

Local utility outages are possible.

Secure loose objects.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Very heavy rain is expected.

When: Today through Tuesday night.

Where: West Vancouver Island from Port Renfrew to the Brooks Peninsula, Inland Vancouver Island, west of Port Alberni, Sproat Lake, Highway 4.

Remarks: A strong frontal system sets up off the West Coast today and persists through Tuesday night, bringing a prolonged period of heavy rain as well as strong winds to the west coast of Vancouver Island. 

Rainfall amounts of 100 - 200 mm are expected, with locally higher amounts possible.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 23 at 8:55PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to
rise through Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue a
gradual rise through the week, and may approach its record flood.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Monday was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising through Major
Flood Stage, reaching 6.1 feet late this week. Additional rises
are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Tuesday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Winter weather travel statement in effect.

What:
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow and local blowing snow.
Local snowfall amounts of 5 cm.

When:
Tonight into early Tuesday morning.

Additional Information:
Lake effect showers and flurries off Lake Huron are expected to intensify and fully change over to snow this evening. Although snowfall amounts are not expected to be significant, visibility may very poor under lake effect snow bands. Conditions are expected to improve Tuesday morning.

Motorists should expect hazardous winter driving conditions and adjust travel plans accordingly. Visibility may be suddenly reduced at times in heavy snow.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. If visibility is reduced while driving, slow down, watch for tail lights ahead and be prepared to stop.

For road conditions and other traveller information from the Ministry of Transportation, visit https://www.ontario.ca/511, https://x.com/511Ontario, or call 5-1-1.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by strong winds and large waves are expected, beginning on Tuesday and lasting for several days.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tide on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.  

Water levels are expected to rise day over day, peaking on Thursday.  This statement will be upgraded to a Coastal Flooding Warning for some regions as the event draws nearer.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Allow extra time for travel. Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snow squall warning
properties.rawText:
Snow squalls off Georgian Bay tonight.

What:
Local snowfall amounts of 10 to 15 cm.
Reduced visibility in areas of heavier snow and local blowing snow.

When:
Tonight into early Tuesday morning.

Where:
Areas south of Georgian Bay, particularly between Barrie and Meaford.

Additional Information:
Lake effect flurries continue tonight. Higher snowfall amounts are possible if a snow squall becomes stationary for a long period of time. Conditions are expected to improve Tuesday morning.

The most significant snowfall should remain west of the city of Barrie and the Highway 400 corridor.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Roads and walkways will likely be difficult to navigate due to accumulating snow.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · coastal flooding warning
properties.rawText:
This warning is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by significant wind and waves are expected, exceeding highest astronomical tide.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides lasting for several days.

When:
During high tide on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to parts of the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Roads, walkways, seawalls and causeways may be difficult to navigate due to flooding and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Damage to anchored or beached boats, wharfs, boat houses or fishing stages along the shoreline is likely.

Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 24 at 8:56AM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 853 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides forecast each day are (all times local
time):
* Port Chicago: 2.2 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 11:36 AM
Mon 11/23, 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, 2.6 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26.
* West Sacramento: 2.2 ft above normal (6.6 ft MLLW) at 2:49
PM Mon 11/23, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM
Tue 11/24, 2.4 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, and 2.3 ft above normal (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/28.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 24 at 11:54AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns at Deland to
rise through Major Flood Stage. The river is forecast to continue a
gradual rise through the week, and may approach its record flood.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 5.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 AM EST Tuesday was 5.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.2 feet early Sunday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Significant snowfall, strong winds, and local blowing snow are possible.

Locations: Postville-Makkovik.

Potential snowfall: 10 to 15 cm.

Time span: ending this afternoon. 

Potential impacts include:
- hazardous travelling conditions
- scattered utility outages

Remarks: Strong northeasterly winds accompanying the snow may reduce visibility at times in blowing snow. Conditions will improve this afternoon as the snow tapers off.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by strong winds and large waves are expected, beginning today and lasting for several days.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tides today, Wednesday and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.  

Water levels are expected to rise day over day, peaking on Thursday.  This statement will be upgraded to a Coastal Flooding Warning for some regions as the event draws nearer.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Very heavy rain is expected.

When: Today and tonight.

Where: West Vancouver Island from Port Renfrew to the Brooks Peninsula, Inland Vancouver Island (from Lake Cowichan to Gold River, Highway 4).

Remarks: A strong frontal system continues impacting Vancouver Island today and tonight, bringing a prolonged period of heavy rain as well as strong winds. 

Rainfall amounts of 100 to 200 mm are expected, with locally higher amounts possible.

Rainfall rates will ease Wednesday morning but another potent storm arrives late Wednesday afternoon bringing a new round of significant precipitation and strong winds.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Allow extra time for travel. Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: West Vancouver Island; Inland Vancouver Island

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

When: Today and tonight.

Where: East Vancouver Island from Fanny Bay to Duncan, Highway 19.

Remarks: A strong frontal system continues impacting Vancouver Island today and tonight, bringing heavy rain and moderate to strong winds. Total rainfall amounts are expected to reach 30 to 60 mm by early Wednesday morning.

Rainfall rates will ease on Wednesday but another potent storm is expected to bring additional heavy rain and strong winds beginning Wednesday night.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas.

Allow extra time for travel. Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Blizzard conditions have developed. Poor visibility in blowing snow will continue until this afternoon.

Limit travel and outdoor activities, if possible. Protect yourself from wind, cold and disorientation by staying sheltered, indoors or with your vehicle.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · blizzard warning
properties.rawText:
Persistent blizzard conditions with very poor visibility in blowing snow are expected.

What:
- Sustained winds near 80 km/h.
- Wind gusts of 100 km/h.
- Blowing snow causing near zero visibility.

When:
Today and lasting potentially until Thursday evening.

Where:
- Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

Additional information:
Strong winds near Rock River are expected to further develop this afternoon. Winds will reach sustained speeds near 80 km/h with gusts reaching 100 km/h. These winds will remain strong tonight, and will moderate slightly late Wednesday evening. Winds are expected to pick up again on Thursday, once again with sustained wind speeds of 70 km/h and gusts up to 80 km/h. Visibility will likely be reduced to near zero due to blowing snow.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Road closures are possible.

Protect yourself from wind, cold and disorientation by staying sheltered, indoors or with your vehicle.

Blizzard warnings are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to YTstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #YTStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · coastal flooding warning
properties.rawText:
This warning is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by significant wind and waves are expected, exceeding highest astronomical tide.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides lasting for several days.

When:
During high tides today, Wednesday and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to parts of the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Roads, walkways, seawalls and causeways may be difficult to navigate due to flooding and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Damage to anchored or beached boats, wharfs, boat houses or fishing stages along the shoreline is likely.

Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 24 at 7:53PM EST until November 24 at 9:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL

SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from west end of Seven Mile Bridge to south of
Halfmoon Shoal 20 to 60 nm out...

* Until 900 PM EST.

* At 752 PM EST, a strong thunderstorm with possible waterspouts was
located 38 nm south of Wood's Wall East Crack, moving northwest at
5 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats, cause
considerable damage to vessels and create suddenly higher
waves. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly
higher waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.
