properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 24 at 4:29PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns Above Lake
Harney near Geneva to remain within Major Flood Stage. River levels
are forecast to hold near a crest through Wednesday before beginning
a very slow decline within Major flood stage later in the week and
into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Above Lake Harney...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river crest has surpassed its previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 10.8 feet, Water covers State Road 46 and it may
become impassable near Jungle Road and Prevatt Road. Standing water
on secondary roads near the river deepens to more than three feet
in some areas. Flooding becomes more significant to structures and
marinas from above Lake Harney to the Lake Jesup area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 PM EST Tuesday the stage was 13.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 PM EST Tuesday was 13.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 11.9 feet Tuesday,
December 01.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 24 at 1:24PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 121 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5
ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW
(7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue
11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3
ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW
(6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/28.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 24 at 12:02PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin has caused levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to rise through Major Flood Stage. The
river is forecast to slowly rise mid week, remaining steady around
4.3 to 4.4 feet through late week and into the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 4.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:30 AM EST Tuesday was 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 4.4 feet
early Thursday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EST.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by strong winds and large waves are expected this week.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tides Wednesday and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.  

Water levels are expected to rise day over day, peaking on Thursday.  This statement will be upgraded to a Coastal Flooding Warning for some regions as the event draws nearer.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Quesnel due to elevated coarse particulate matter.

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoor activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Conditions may improve throughout the day as weather patterns change.

The next update will be on November 25, 2026 and posted to the province's Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

properties.title: Yellow warning · coastal flooding warning
properties.rawText:
This warning is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by significant wind and waves are expected, exceeding highest astronomical tide.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides lasting for several days.

When:
During high tides Wednesday and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to parts of the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Roads, walkways, seawalls and causeways may be difficult to navigate due to flooding and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Damage to anchored or beached boats, wharfs, boat houses or fishing stages along the shoreline is likely.

Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 4:17AM EST until November 25 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL

SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL from 20 to 60 NM
excluding the territorial waters of Bahamas...

* Until 500 AM EST.

* At 417 AM EST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 41 nm east of Floyd's Wall Northeast,
moving north at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 40 knots.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* The severe thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.

Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.title: Yellow warning · air quality warning
properties.rawText:
Elevated pollution levels are expected or occurring.

The Ministry of Environment and Parks in collaboration with the Northern Health Authority has issued an Air Quality Warning for Quesnel due to elevated coarse particulate matter.

Exposure to coarse particulate matter is particularly a concern for infants, older adults, individuals with chronic conditions (such as asthma, COPD, heart disease, and diabetes) or respiratory infections, and those who are pregnant.

Postpone or reduce strenuous outdoor activities until the warning has ended. Spend time indoors in a space with filtered air. Monitor your symptoms and seek prompt medical attention if needed.

Conditions may improve throughout the day as weather patterns change.

The next update will be on November 25, 2026 and posted to the province's Air Quality Warnings webpage.

Visit https://www.airhealth.ca for information on how to reduce your health risk and your personal contribution to pollution levels, as well as for current and forecast AQHI values.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada.

Issued by Environment Canada and the B.C. Ministry of Environment and Parks

properties.title: Yellow warning · wind warning
properties.rawText:
A prolonged period of strong winds continues.

When: Tonight.

Where: Areas of Greater Victoria near Juan de Fuca and Haro Straits, Southern Gulf Island.

Remarks:
A vigorous frontal system continues impacting Vancouver Island tonight. Strong southeasterly winds gusting up to 90 km/h at times are forecast.

Winds will remain moderately gusty Wednesday morning but below warning criteria and gradually ease through the day. Another potent storm arrives Wednesday night bringing strong southeasterly winds once again.

Local utility outages are possible.

Secure loose objects. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:32PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels on
the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood Stage.
The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest this
weekend, reaching 6.4 feet, where it is expected to linger into early
next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river is forecast to rise above the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:30 PM EST Wednesday was 5.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 6.4 feet Saturday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1100 AM EST.

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 945 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed
11/25, +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, +2.2
ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.7 ft MHHW
(6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed
11/25, +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, +2.1
ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, and +1.8 ft MHHW
(6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25,
+7.4 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26, +7.3 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27,
+6.9 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28 and +7.0 ft at 7:00 PM Sun
11/29.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131

Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 25 at 9:30AM PST until November 27 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olypics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this afternoon to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast. This approaches the flood of
record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM PST Wednesday the stage was 15.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage this afternoon
to 17.9 feet late tonight. It will then fall below flood stage
late Friday morning. Further rises through the weekend are
likely, with exceeding flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 530 PM PST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Strong winds are expected.

When: Tonight.

Where: Inland Vancouver Island near Port Alberni.

Remarks: Another storm in a series of potent weather systems will arrive tonight. Southerly winds will funnel up the Alberni Inlet this evening. Wind gusts will peak near 70 km/h late this evening and near midnight before easing overnight.

Local utility outages are possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by strong winds and large waves are expected this week.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tides today and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.  

Water levels are expected to rise day over day, peaking on Thursday.  This statement will be upgraded to a Coastal Flooding Warning for some regions as the event draws nearer.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is expected.

When: Tonight and Thursday morning.

Where: Howe Sound, Whistler, Sea-to-Sky Highway, Metro Vancouver - northeastern section and North Shore.

Remarks: A strong frontal system will arrive tonight. Heavy rain will bring an additional 30 to 60 mm of rain to what has already fallen in recent days. Moderate rainfall rates of 5 to 8 mm/h are possible at times. A risk of thunderstorms is forecast for Thursday morning near Metro Vancouver.

Multiple hazards accompany this storm including King Tides, strong winds, and an already drenched landscape from recent weather.

Water will likely pool on roads and in low-lying areas.

Allow extra time for travel. Watch for washouts near rivers, creeks and culverts.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.rawText:
Persistent blizzard conditions with very poor visibility in blowing snow continue.

What:
- Sustained winds near 80 km/h.
- Wind gusts of 100 km/h.
- Blowing snow causing near zero visibility.

When:

Where:
- Dempster Highway near the Richardson Mountains.

properties.title: Yellow warning · coastal flooding warning
properties.rawText:
This warning is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Elevated ocean water levels accompanied by significant wind and waves are expected, exceeding highest astronomical tide.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides lasting for several days.

When:
During high tides today and Thursday.

Additional information:
A series of deep low pressure systems will track across the offshore waters this week, bringing storm surge and large waves to parts of the BC Coast. This will coincide with a run of king tides, elevating water levels 20 to 50 cm higher than the highest astronomical tides.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Roads, walkways, seawalls and causeways may be difficult to navigate due to flooding and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Damage to anchored or beached boats, wharfs, boat houses or fishing stages along the shoreline is likely.

Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Heavy rain is expected.

When: This afternoon and tonight.

Where: West Vancouver Island, North Vancouver Island (near Port Alice), and Inland Vancouver Island.

Remarks: The final storm in a series of potent weather systems arrives today. Heavy rain will bring an additional 50 to 100 mm of rain to what has already fallen in recent days. Moderate to heavy rainfall rates of 5-15 mm/h are expected and there is the additional risk of thunderstorms late overnight into Thursday morning.

Multiple hazards accompany this storm including King Tides, strong winds, and an already drenched landscape from recent storms.

Localized flooding is likely. Some roads may become impassable. Significant property damage is likely. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts. Be prepared to evacuate. Listen for direction from local authorities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning
properties.rawText:
Special Marine Warning issued November 25 at 9:12PM EST until November 25 at 10:00PM EST by NWS Key West FL

SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Hawk Channel and Straits of Florida from Ocean Reef to Craig Key
out 20 nm...

* Until 1000 PM EST.

* At 912 PM EST, a strong thunderstorm was located over Islamorada
Hump, moving northeast at 35 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* Locations in the warning include...
Key Largo Dry Rocks, Mosquito Bank Light, South Rips, Islamorada
Hump, French Ref, Spiegel Grove, and Grecian Rocks.

Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

Intense and continuous lightning is occurring with this storm. Stay
low, or go below. Lower VHF antenna, outriggers, fishing rods, and
umbrellas.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 25 at 8:32PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels
on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood
Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest
this weekend, reaching 6.4 feet, where it is expected to linger into
early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Wednesday the stage was 5.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Wednesday was 5.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise through Major Flood
Stage, reaching 6.4 feet late this weekend. The river is then
forecast to remain steady through early next week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at noon EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:17PM PST until November 27 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops, will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this evening to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow
morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning.
Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding
flood stage possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1030 PM PST.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Snow, heavy at times, is expected.

Where: Highway 3 - Paulson Summit to Kootenay Pass.

When: Overnight tonight until overnight Thursday.

What: 15 to 25 cm of snow.

Remarks: A moisture-laden system will push into southern B.C. tonight. Snow will begin near midnight and will become heavy at times overnight. The heaviest snow is expected to ease by early Thursday afternoon, however, light to moderate snow is expected to continue through Thursday night. Strong southerly winds will accompany the heavy snow, occasionally reducing visibility significantly.

Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Weather in the mountains can change suddenly resulting in hazardous driving conditions.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Allow extra time for travel. The site https://shiftintowinter.ca/ reminds drivers to know before you go. Adjust to winter driving behaviour and use winter tires and chains.

Road conditions are available at https://www.drivebc.ca/.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

Additional information:
A strong frontal system will track across the B.C. coast tonight and Thursday, bringing storm surge and large waves. This will coincide with king tides, elevating water levels 30 to 50 cm higher than astronomical tides to produce moderate to significant coastal flooding.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Unsafe driving conditions due to flooded roads and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks, is possible. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Ground floors of some properties and parts of communities may be affected by flooding.

Residents should take immediate action to protect life and property. Heed advice from emergency management organizations. Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 25 at 10:13PM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight plus an additional 2-4 inches
of rain, with snow levels well above mountain tops, will drive the
Skokomish River above flood stage this evening to above Moderate
flood.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 PM PST Wednesday the stage was 17.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 PM PST Wednesday was 17.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 17.9 feet late tomorrow
morning. It will then fall below flood stage late Friday morning.
Further rises through the weekend are likely, with exceeding
flood stage possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

What:

properties.title: Yellow warning · coastal flooding warning
properties.rawText:
This warning is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Moderate flooding along coastlines and low-lying areas due to storm surge, large waves and high tides.

What:
Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

When:
During high tides today.

Additional information:
A strong frontal system will track across the B.C. coast tonight and Thursday, bringing storm surge and large waves. This will coincide with king tides, elevating water levels 30 to 60 cm higher than astronomical tides to produce moderate to significant coastal flooding.

Consult tides.gc.ca for local tide calendars.

Unsafe driving conditions due to flooded roads and/or debris, such as driftwood and rocks, is possible. Coastal erosion is likely in sensitive areas, such as tidal flats, estuaries, dunes, beaches or barrier islands. Ground floors of some properties and parts of communities may be affected by flooding.

Residents should take immediate action to protect life and property. Heed advice from emergency management organizations. Prepare your property by moving valuables and harmful chemicals from your basement or crawl space to safe, elevated locations. Secure loose objects that may be carried away by water. Stay away from the shore to prevent being swept off rocks, injured by heavy objects such as rocks or driftwood or pulled out to sea.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Orange warning · rainfall warning
properties.rawText:
Heavy rain is occurring.

When: Tonight.

Where: East Vancouver Island.

Remarks: The final storm in a series of potent weather systems arrives tonight. Heavy rain will bring an additional 30 to 60 mm of rain to what has already fallen in recent days. Moderate rainfall rates up to 5 to 10 mm/h are possible.

Heavy rain will ease to a few showers late overnight.

Multiple hazards accompany this storm including King Tides, strong winds, and an already drenched landscape from recent weather.

Localized flooding is likely. Some roads may become impassable. Significant property damage is likely. Landslides may occur in vulnerable areas such as steep slopes, deforested areas or recent burn scars.

Stay away from rivers, creeks and culverts. Be prepared to evacuate. Listen for direction from local authorities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.rawText:
Tornado Warning issued November 26 at 11:58AM PST until November 26 at 12:15PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

TORSEW

The National Weather Service in Seattle has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Central King County in west central Washington...

* Until 1215 PM PST.

* At 1140 AM PST, a landspout was located near Renton, moving east
at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Weather spotters confirmed landspout.

IMPACT...Possible damage to mobile homes, roofs, and vehicles.

* The tornado will be near...
Snoqualmie around 1205 PM PST.

Other locations impacted by this tornadic thunderstorm include Fall
City, Mirrormont, Tanner, and Hobart.

To repeat, a tornado is on the ground. TAKE COVER NOW! Move to a
basement or an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy
building. Avoid windows. If you are outdoors or in a vehicle, move to
the closest substantial shelter and protect yourself from flying
debris.

To report severe weather contact your nearest law enforcement agency.
They will send your report to the National Weather Service office in
Seattle.

Flood Warning issued November 26 at 9:24AM PST until November 26 at 6:00PM PST by NWS Sacramento CA

* WHAT...Coastal Flooding from abnormally high tides.

* WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 918 AM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26, +2.2 ft MHHW (7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27, +1.7
ft MHHW (6.6 ft MLLW) at 3:44 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.2 ft MHHW
(6.1 ft MLLW) at 4:53 PM Sun 11/29.
* West Sacramento: +2.3 ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu
11/26, +2.1 ft MHHW (6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27, +1.8
ft MHHW (6.2 ft MLLW) at 6:59 PM Sat 11/28, and +1.4 ft MHHW
(5.8 ft MLLW) at 8:03 PM Sun 11/29.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.5 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27, +7.3 ft at 6:00 PM Sat 11/28,
+6.7 ft at 9:00 AM Sun 11/29, and +6.3 ft at 9:00 AM Mon
11/30.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1

Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 26 at 4:34AM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1245 PM PST.

This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Moderate storm surge
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Coastal flooding due to storm surge and large waves coinciding with king tides.

Ice build-up due to freezing rain is expected.

What:

Wind gusts up to 60 km/h during the onset of freezing rain.

Where:
For higher elevation areas of the Dundalk Highlands.

When:
Beginning this evening and ending Friday morning.

Several hours of freezing rain are possible, particularly for higher terrain along and above the Niagara Escarpment where temperatures are expected to remain just below the freezing mark for much of the night.

Elsewhere, temperatures will likely rise above the freezing mark with less ice build-up is expected as a result.

Wind gusts up to 60 km/h are expected. Any ice build-up combined with strong winds increases the risk of broken tree branches.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 26 at 9:11PM EST until November 28 at 5:00AM EST by NWS Wakefield VA

...The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in North Carolina...

Cashie River Near Windsor affecting Bertie County.

For the Lower Roanoke Basin...including Windsor...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Cashie River near Windsor.

* WHEN...From this evening until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Portions of N. York St, Davis Ball Park and
the Cashie Wetlands Walk begin to flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 8.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.6 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage late
tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.6
feet on 12/25/2014.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 915 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 26 at 8:58PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause levels
on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady within Major Flood
Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Campground are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 4.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Thursday was 4.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain generally steady
between 4.3 and 4.4 feet through early next week.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 26 at 8:38PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends are forecast to
follow a very slow decline through Major Flood Stage into the weekend
and through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Thursday was 18.4 feet.

week.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 26 at 3:17PM PST until November 27 at 3:34PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast to continue. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM PST Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM PST Thursday was 17.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to hover near a
crest of 17.9 feet through this evening. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight PST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Prolonged period of freezing rain is expected.

Locations: Bathurst and Chaleur Region, and inland parts of eastern New Brunswick.

Potential freezing rain duration: 3 to 5 hours.

Time span: Friday morning until Friday near noon.

Potential impacts include:
- Hazardous driving conditions
- Slippery sidewalks, walkways, and other outdoor surfaces

Remarks: A deepening low pressure system is expected to bring a prolonged period of freezing rain. Although freezing rain may be intermittent in some locations, ice accumulation could become significant over time. 

Areas along the coasts are likely to experience rain. Freezing rain is most likely in inland regions and over higher terrain. 

Freezing rain is expected to transition to rain as milder air moves in Friday afternoon. Improvement may be slower within inland valley locations and over higher terrain, where temperatures are forecast to remain colder.

Even modest amounts of freezing rain can result in hazardous ice accumulation over time. Rural and hilly roads may become particularly slippery, potentially making travel and access to some communities difficult.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NBstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NBStorm.

Several hours of freezing rain will bring 2 to 5 mm of ice build-up, with locally higher amounts possible.
Utility outages are possible.
Wind gusts up to 60 km/h during the onset of freezing rain.

Where:
For higher elevation areas of the Dundalk Highlands.

When:
Beginning this evening and ending Friday morning.

Additional information:
Precipitation associated with an approaching low pressure system will move into the region by this evening. Several hours of freezing rain are possible, particularly for higher terrain along and above the Niagara Escarpment where temperatures are expected to remain just below the freezing mark for much of the night.

Elsewhere, temperatures will likely rise above the freezing mark with less ice build-up expected as a result.

Wind gusts up to 60 km/h are expected. Any ice build-up combined with strong winds increases the risk of broken tree branches.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

Be very careful if walking or driving. Be aware of falling ice and  branches.

Freezing rain is expected.

Locations: western, northwestern, and central New Brunswick.

Freezing rain duration: 4 to 9 hours.
Total freezing rain amounts: 5 to 15 mm.

Time span: Friday morning until Friday afternoon.

Potential impacts include:
- scattered utility outages
- hazardous driving conditions
- disruptions to transportation services
- slippery surfaces

Remarks: Ice accumulations could approach 5 mm in some areas. Improvement may be slower in valley locations and over higher terrain, where temperatures will remain colder. 

Even small amounts of freezing rain can make travel difficult. Even relatively short periods of freezing rain could result in hazardous ice accumulation. Rural travel routes may also become icy, potentially making access difficult.

Allow extra time for travel and be prepared for changing road conditions. Be prepared for possible delays or disruptions to transportation services. Those accessing remote cabins or backcountry areas should consider the potential for icy access routes.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. There may be a significant impact on rush hour traffic. Icy surfaces could be difficult to detect. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

Be very careful if walking or driving.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Ice build-up due to freezing rain is expected this evening. 

Freezing rain will taper off tonight.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. Icy surfaces could be difficult to detect. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

Be very careful if walking or driving.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ABstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #ABStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 27 at 4:19AM EST until November 27 at 8:00AM EST by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Prince William County in northern Virginia...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EST.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 418 AM EST, water levels on Cedar Run at Aden are crested and
are in Minor Flood stage. Flooding is ongoing.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Cedar Run, Goose Run, Goslin Run and Lucky Run. Flooding impacts
will continue, but no additional rainfall is expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Prince William County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

forecast.

the Genito Creek Bridge due to high water.

- At 3:45 AM EST Friday the stage was 15.1 feet.

tomorrow evening.

feet on 02/02/1957.

forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

- At 10:30 PM PST Thursday the stage was 17.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 PM PST Thursday was 18.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to hover near a
crest of 17.8 feet through this evening. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow morning.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
Prolonged period of freezing rain is expected.

Locations: Bathurst and Chaleur Region, and inland parts of eastern New Brunswick.

Potential freezing rain duration: 2 to 4 hours.

Time span: beginning this morning and ending near noon.

Potential impacts include:
- Hazardous driving conditions
- Slippery sidewalks, walkways, and other outdoor surfaces

Remarks: A deepening low pressure system is expected to bring a prolonged period of freezing rain. Although freezing rain may be intermittent in some locations, ice accumulation could become significant over time. 

Areas along the coasts are likely to experience rain. Freezing rain is most likely in inland regions and over higher terrain. 

Freezing rain is expected to transition to rain as milder air moves in this afternoon. Improvement may be slower within inland valley locations and over higher terrain, where temperatures are forecast to remain colder.

Even modest amounts of freezing rain can result in hazardous ice accumulation over time. Rural and hilly roads may become particularly slippery, potentially making travel and access to some communities difficult.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NBstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NBStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Freezing rain is expected.

Locations: western, northwestern, and central New Brunswick.

Freezing rain duration: 4 to 6 hours.
Total freezing rain amounts: 5 to 15 mm.

Time span: until this afternoon.

Potential impacts include:
- scattered utility outages
- hazardous driving conditions
- disruptions to transportation services
- slippery surfaces

Remarks: Ice accumulations could approach 5 mm in some areas. Improvement may be slower in valley locations and over higher terrain, where temperatures will remain colder. 

Even small amounts of freezing rain can make travel difficult. Even relatively short periods of freezing rain could result in hazardous ice accumulation. Rural travel routes may also become icy, potentially making access difficult.

Allow extra time for travel and be prepared for changing road conditions. Be prepared for possible delays or disruptions to transportation services. Those accessing remote cabins or backcountry areas should consider the potential for icy access routes.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. There may be a significant impact on rush hour traffic. Icy surfaces could be difficult to detect. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

Be very careful if walking or driving.

Freezing rain warnings are issued when rain falling in sub-zero temperatures is expected to create ice build-up.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NBstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NBStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Ice build-up due to freezing rain continues.

What:
Several hours of freezing rain will bring 2 to 5 mm of ice build-up, with locally higher amounts possible.
Utility outages are possible.
Wind gusts up to 60 km/h.

Where:
Higher elevation areas of the Oak Ridges including the townships of Alnwick, Percy, Haldimand and areas along Highway 115 between the 407 and Highway 7.

When:
Ending this morning.

Additional information:
Several hours of freezing rain are expected, particularly for the higher terrain over the Oak Ridges where temperatures are expected to remain just below the freezing mark for much of the night.

Areas closer to Lake Ontario should see little to no ice build-up with temperatures remaining above freezing.

Wind gusts up to 60 km/h are expected. Any ice build-up combined with strong winds increases the risk of broken tree branches.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. There is risk of injury due to slips and falls.

Be aware of falling ice and  branches. Stay away from fallen power lines.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Massachusetts...

Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles.
Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EST Friday the stage was 7.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 8.5 feet early tomorrow
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage Sunday evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 100 AM EST.

properties.title: special weather statement
properties.rawText:
What: Freezing rain possible

When: This evening

Additional information:
Local freezing rain is possible locally Friday evening in some areas of eastern Quebec. Surfaces such as roads or sidewalks could be particularly slippery.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
What: A few hours of freezing rain

When: Today

Additional information: Ice accretion will be greater in valleys where cold air accumulates.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. Icy surfaces could be difficult to detect.

Freezing rain warnings are issued when rain falling in sub-zero temperatures is expected to create ice build-up.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
Freezing rain is expected.

An low pressure system is spreading an area of freezing rain across portions of central and northern Manitoba this morning.

The threat for freezing rain will end this afternoon.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. Local utility outages are possible.

Freezing rain warnings are issued when rain falling in sub-zero temperatures is expected to create ice build-up.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #MBStorm.

properties.title: Yellow warning · storm surge warning
properties.rawText:
Higher than normal water levels are expected near the coast this evening.

The combinaison of:
- of moderate winds from the northeast
- a moderate surge set-up, and
- a high tidal range could cause minor overwash along the coast on Friday evening.

Coastal flooding is possible along the shore.

This warning is issued when high water levels pose a threat to coastal regions due to tides, storm surge and/or waves.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

properties.title: Gale Warning
properties.rawText:
Gale Warning issued November 27 at 9:46PM EST until November 28 at 1:00PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA

* WHAT...West winds 25 to 35 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and seas
9 to 14 ft.

* WHERE...Waters from Fenwick Island DE to Chintoteague VA from
20 to 60 NM and Waters from Chincoteague VA to Parramore
Island VA from 20 to 60 NM.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 27 at 8:34PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends are forecast to
follow a very slow decline through Major Flood Stage into the weekend
and through next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Friday the stage was 18.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Friday was 18.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to show a very slow decline from
18.2 feet to 17.8 feet late this week and through next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1115 AM EST.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 27 at 1:14PM PST until November 28 at 10:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:30 PM PST Friday the stage was 17.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage early tomorrow
afternoon to 16.3 feet late tomorrow evening.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.1
feet on 12/15/1999.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM PST.

properties.title: Yellow warning · freezing rain warning
properties.rawText:
What: A few hours of freezing rain.

When: This evening.

Additional information: Liquid precipitation will turn into snow this evening.

Roads and walkways will likely become icy and slippery. Icy surfaces could be difficult to detect.

Freezing rain warnings are issued when rain falling in sub-zero temperatures is expected to create ice build-up.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 28 at 5:50AM EST until November 30 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Bristol and Plymouth
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...Until late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles.
Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:45 AM EST Saturday the stage was 8.3 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 4:45 AM EST Saturday was 8.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.4 feet
this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage late tomorrow
evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 600 PM EST.

properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 27 at 11:13PM PST until November 28 at 10:00AM PST by NWS Seattle WA

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause widespread
flooding of pasture lands, with water flowing quickly over West
Bourgault Road and Skokomish Valley Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM PST Friday the stage was 16.6 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:30 PM PST Friday was 17.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall below flood stage just after
midnight tonight to 16.0 feet late tonight. It will then rise to
16.3 feet late Sunday morning. It will fall to 16.1 feet late
Sunday evening. It will then rise above flood stage early Monday
morning to 16.8 feet late Monday evening. It will fall below
flood stage again Tuesday morning.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.8
feet on 03/13/2003.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1000 AM PST.

properties.title: coastal flooding statement
properties.rawText:
This statement is in effect for parts of the coast due to the following hazard(s): 
- Large waves
- Very high tides
- Higher than normal water levels

Locations: southwestern shore of Nova Scotia from Yarmouth to Port Medway.

Time span: this morning until afternoon.

High tide: 10:00 A.M. to 2:00 P.M. today.

Remarks: The potential exists for coastal waters to  exceed the highest astronomical tide when storm surge combines with strong wave action near high tide.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NSstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NSStorm.
properties.stationOrArea: Coastline of Queens County; Coastline of Shelburne County; Coastline of Yarmouth County

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Significant snowfall is expected in some areas.

Location: Green Bay - White Bay.

Total snowfall: 5 to 10 cm, except 15 to 20 cm over the Baie Verte Peninsula, as well as Hampden to Jackson's Arm.

Time span: this afternoon until Sunday morning.

Remarks: Precipitation will fall mainly as snow inland and in the vicinity of White Bay, while a mixture of snow and rain will occur elsewhere. The snow is expected to be wet and heavy.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Allow extra time for travel.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow warning · Wreckhouse wind warning
properties.rawText:
Damaging winds are expected.

Maximum wind gusts: easterly 100 km/h in the Wreckhouse area.

Time span: near noon today.

Driving conditions will likely be difficult. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind.

Wind warnings are issued when there is a significant risk of damaging winds.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:31AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels
on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood
Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest
this weekend, reaching 6.5 feet, then continuing to 6.6 feet early
next week where it is expected to linger into at least mid next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The river is forecast to rise above the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM EST Saturday the stage was 6.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending

weekend and through next week.

properties.title: Flood Warning
properties.rawText:
Flood Warning issued November 28 at 8:17AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall across the upper St. Johns River has caused levels
near Cocoa to remain within Major Flood Stage, well above its
previous record flood stage. The river level trends are forecast to
follow a very slow decline through Major Flood Stage through next
week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The crest has exceeded the previous flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 AM EST Saturday the stage was 18.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 AM EST Saturday was 18.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is forecast to show a very slow decline from
18.2 feet to 17.7 feet from this weekend and through next week.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM EST.

.Past heavy rainfall working its way through the basin will cause
levels on the St Johns River at Astor to remain steady within Major
Flood Stage between 4.3 and 4.4 feet well into next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 4.5 feet, Major widespread and long duration flooding
occurs, with water rescues and evacuations necessary. Most
low-lying homes become uninhabitable due to 2 to 3 feet water depth
in many areas of the community on or near the river. Water reaches
Front Street south of SR-40. Areas off of Riveredge Drive are
inaccessible. Water surrounds and enters homes on Riverview Drive
and Claire Street. Most areas near the Astor Landing Camptround are
inaccessible due to knee-deep water.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · fog advisory
properties.rawText:
Near-zero visibility in fog is expected.

When:
Now until this afternoon.

Where:
Inland sections of the North Coast.

Remarks:
Areas of dense fog have developed this morning significantly reducing visibilities. The dense fog will dissipate  this afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced at times.

If driving, turn on your lights, slow down and maintain a safe following distance.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

properties.title: Yellow advisory · blowing snow advisory
properties.rawText:
Snow and strong winds will lead to poor visibility in blowing snow in some locations.

Locations: Northern Peninsula East.

Total snowfall: near 5 cm, except 10 to 15 cm south of Hare Bay.

Maximum wind gusts: northeasterly 60 km/h.

Time span: tonight.

Remarks: Conditions are expected to be poorest south of Hare Bay, where the gusty winds will coincide with the most snowfall.

Travel will likely be hazardous in some locations.

Consider postponing non-essential travel and outdoor activities until conditions improve.

Blowing snow advisories are issued when widespread poor visibility in blowing snow is expected.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow warning · snowfall warning
properties.rawText:
Significant snowfall is expected in some areas.

Location: Green Bay - White Bay.

Total snowfall: 5 to 10 cm, except 15 to 20 cm over the Baie Verte Peninsula, as well as Hampden to Jackson's Arm.

Time span: this afternoon until Sunday morning.

Remarks: Precipitation will fall mainly as snow inland and in the vicinity of White Bay, while a mixture of snow and rain will occur elsewhere. The snow is expected to be wet and heavy.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Allow extra time for travel.

Snowfall warnings are issued when significant impacts are expected due to snowfall accumulations.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NLstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #NLwx.

properties.title: Yellow warning · storm surge warning
properties.rawText:
Higher than normal water levels with large waves are expected near the coast Saturday afternoon.


The combinaison of:
- moderate winds from the northeast
- a weak surge set-up
- a high tidal range
risk of causing a minor wave surge along the coast on Saturday afternoon.

Additional information:
Coastal flooding is likely to occur along the coastline.
Coastal erosion is possible in vulnerable areas.

This warning is issued when high water levels pose a threat to coastal regions due to tides, storm surge and/or waves.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to QCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #QCStorm.
